dedupe_keys.name: the eco social water tariff in dunkerque climate adapt case study

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the eco-social water tariff introduced in Dunkerque, France, in 2012 to curb consumption under water scarcity while keeping water affordable for low-income households. The three-tier progressive tariff charges 1.29 euros per m3 for the first 80 m3 a year per household, considered vital, 2.40 euros up to 200 m3, and 3.18 euros beyond, with extra support for the most vulnerable; setup cost about 180,000 euros and billing adds 1.5 cents per m3. Coverage is the Dunkerque area. The page is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal, published in 2024 and updated in 2026. Caveats: the latest specific data are from a 2017 report, and the outcome figures are the scheme's own assessment. Simulation uses: price-based demand scenarios for water supply planning under drought. Related records: the Zaragoza water saving case study (case_study-zaragoza-water-saving-city).
name: The eco-social water tariff in Dunkerque (Climate-ADAPT case study)
outcomes: 80 per cent of consumers pay the same or less than before, overall consumption fell, and about 80 per cent of higher-tier consumers reduced their use.

sources.note: Climate-ADAPT REST record: tariff tiers and prices, 2012 start, setup 180,000 EUR, 1.5 cents per m3, outcomes from 2017 report, published 2024-11-05, modified 2026-08-25
